summary: Adds silver.temp_hdx and silver.temp_hdx_categorized, built beside silver.hdx but without the double-entry and accession holds, so every form shows up labeled with its entry type.

nodes.note: Per field; NULL on a single entry.

edges.label: temp_dag("hdx", …)
edges.description: Each temp_dag call registers one DAG. temp_load_hdx is scheduled on the bronze HDX window extracts plus silver.slim; temp_load_hdx_categorized on the temp hdx asset.

edges.label: run_model(layer=TEMP, buckets)
edges.description: The build task resolves the window from the watermark (or the window_start param) and hands it to run_model with layer=TEMP and the run's buckets param.

edges.label: per bucket
edges.description: run_model renders each step under temp/hdx in order, once per bucket of keys; 010 maps is the first.
staging.temp_hdx_maps holds the mappings to rebuild this run; 020 finds which of their forms, or mappings, are now tombstoned.

edges.label: entry_type(...)
edges.description: The spine's SELECT calls the entry_type macro on its joined rows, so each form gets its label in the same pass.

edges.label: verdicts
edges.description: 080 joins each form's verdict: its accession number, or the reason it would be withheld.
The spine's entry_type travels with each form into 080 and onto every field row.
The per-field agree flag decides whether the agreed value can be the complete value.
080 writes the finished field rows to staging.temp_hdx_source; 090 upserts them into silver.temp_hdx by row_key.

edges.label: reads silver.temp_hdx
edges.description: The form view reads one form's field rows from silver.temp_hdx: both entries, the complete value and the agree flag per field.
Each route calls the service: summary, protocols and forms for the list; form for one mapping.
With the deleted forms known, 030 gathers the field values for every entry of the mappings in scope.
The spine joins each mapping to its enrollment, subject, protocol and both entries, reading ACC_ID from the entry data and skipping deleted forms.
050 reads the audit history of the spine's entries to find the latest superuser resolution of each field.
060 gathers the accession evidence (raw value, ACC and external fields, bridge) for every spine form, one row per form.

edges.label: superuser choices
edges.description: A resolved field's superuser choice wins over both entries when 080 picks the complete value.
070 is just a SELECT over the candidates; PYTHON_STEPS routes it to Python instead of running it as SQL.

edges.label: PYTHON_STEPS → temp_gate
edges.description: run_step streams the SELECT's rows into hdx.temp_gate, which runs the accession ladder on each and writes verdicts to staging.temp_hdx_accession.
After the upsert, 100 writes a deleted version of every row whose form is in staging.temp_hdx_deleted.

edges.label: temp_load_hdx_categorized
edges.description: When temp_load_hdx finishes it emits the temp hdx asset, which triggers temp_load_hdx_categorized; its 010 finds the forms whose rows landed in the window.
020 pivots each touched form's live field rows into the entry1, entry2 and complete JSON maps.
030 finds touched forms with no live silver.temp_hdx row left, so their categorized row can go.
040 upserts the pivoted forms into silver.temp_hdx_categorized.
050 writes a deleted version for the forms 030 found.

edges.label: template_module(macros/temp_hdx)
edges.description: template_module loads the macro file as a module, so tests can read its column lists rather than repeating them.

edges.label: /dq/hdx-test
edges.description: The HDX test link in the console's top bar opens /dq/hdx-test.

edges.label: render_template
edges.description: The list route renders temp_hdx.html with the counts, filters and the page of forms.

edges.label: render_template
edges.description: The form route renders temp_hdx_form.html with entry 1, entry 2 and complete side by side; an unknown form is a 404.

edges.label: reads categorized
edges.description: Counts and the form list read silver.temp_hdx_categorized, one row per form, filtered by entry type, accession hold and protocol.
